implementation: Reuse canonical encoded rows only for the same immutable cached row tuple; history changes rebuild it. Wire/session/frame trimming and TTL remain independent.
limits: Separate sequential host workloads, not controlled hardware isolation or universal speedup.
Near-byte case has twelve 170000-byte ASCII answer texts (2040000 text bytes), not arbitrary worst-case payload or maximum simultaneous row-and-byte limits.
The same immutable display body/frame is preserved during each sampled unchanged interval. Existing cross-language/malformed/transaction/cache tests pass again.
No native rendering, physical input, gameplay, provider inference, normal history or concurrency acceptance.
